title: Electric force magnitude
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the magnitude of the electric force using F = qE, yielding 2 × 10⁻⁴ N.

title: Electric force direction
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the direction of the force on the positive charge is along the electric field (e.g., to the right).

title: Work calculation
description: Important: The response must correctly apply the work formula W = F * d * cosθ or W = qE * L_AB * cosθ, yielding 2 × 10⁻⁵ J.

title: Potential energy change
description: Important: The response must correctly relate work and change in potential energy using W = -ΔE_p, yielding ΔE_p = -2 × 10⁻⁵ J.

title: Potential difference
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the potential difference using U_AB = W/q or U_AB = E * L_AB * cosθ, yielding 2 × 10³ V.

title: Angle misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the work calculation incorrectly uses the angle (e.g., uses sinθ or 0° instead of 60°).

title: Sign convention error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign relationship between work and potential energy change (W = -ΔE_p) is reversed or omitted.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Award credit for explicitly showing unit analysis or correctly stating units (N, J, V) with answers.
